title: Source learning from Modular Recursive Plugin Pipeline v7

scope.authorization: AUTH-10: user replied go to the concrete catalogue proposal
scope.source_boundary: The nine-file ZIP only; current Docstream requirements are application context, not evidence of source implementation.
scope.method: Manual static review with selected exact excerpts and file/line locators. No source evaluation, browser execution, dependency installation, integration or product correction.
scope.adoption_rule: Catalogue inclusion is not adoption. Do not wholesale lift code, classes, taxonomies, architecture, claimed guarantees or assumptions.
scope.application_status: All application statements are proposals and remain not_adopted.
scope.evidence_limit: Static inspection establishes code structure and branches; predicted runtime effects remain untested. Hashes establish byte identity only.

source.locator_convention: Files are relative to root_entry inside the ZIP, not extracted workspace files. Lines are 1-based LF splits with terminal CR removed and the final empty line retained. Excerpts are exact substrings within the cited range.

taxonomy.status: Assistant working organization approved for this catalogue; not a universal classification or product schema.

categories.lesson: A useful principle supported by the source observation.
categories.anti_lesson: A conclusion or guarantee that should not be inferred from this source.
categories.pattern: A potentially reusable arrangement of responsibilities or behavior.
categories.antipattern: An arrangement unsuitable under the stated application conditions.
categories.structure: A concrete component, record, interface or relationship.
categories.edifice: A larger composition of structures and its operating assumptions.
categories.mechanism: How a behavior is arranged or carried out.
categories.invariant: A condition a future application would need to maintain.
categories.failure_mode: A source-observed gap or a specifically labeled predicted failure.
categories.trade_off: A benefit and cost that depend on purpose or environment.
categories.open_question: A question unresolved by this static review.

application_context.authority: Direct instructions in the current chat; no source-packet or historical TODO grants implementation authority.
constraints: Catalogue lessons and anti-lessons without wholesale adoption.
Native AI-originated documents are the current working assumption; foreign-document reconstruction need not govern the proposed native core.
The user describes direct one-to-one references assembled into words, sentences and paragraphs, with per-system maps including HTML and Python.
Changes produce new streams and retain requested transformations; reduction does not erase their history.
CPU first; later GPU implementation requires a separate scope.
unresolved: Native unit catalogue schema and reference width.
Whether words, sentences and paragraphs are separately interned or only assembled ranges.
Exact codepage contents, return/control semantics and version-binding policy.
Any implementation or runtime validation of the supplied plugin pipeline.

entries.title: Separate definitions from occurrences

source_evidence.observation: Registry metadata uses typeId while runtime nodes also carry instanceId; loaded instances receive distinct counter-based IDs.
A loaded instance is distinguished from its installed type.

interpretation.text: A reusable definition and an occurrence are different identities. The source demonstrates this for processors, not characters or native assembly objects.

application.text: Define native unit identity, assembly occurrence identity and processing occurrence identity separately. Reuse the principle after specifying their own contracts.

limitations: The local counter does not establish durable identity across sessions.
Plugin identity is not automatically a native character reference.
validation_needed: Repeated definitions remain distinguishable from repeated occurrences.
Restart and reference-resolution rules are explicit.

entries.title: A registry key does not freeze a definition

source_evidence.observation: Registering an existing typeId replaces the registry entry without a version check.
An installed factory is also stored by the replaceable type key.

interpretation.text: A repeated name can select a changed definition. The registry alone does not provide the stable meanings needed to withstand redefinition.

application.text: Consider immutable definition identities and explicit version/content binding for native maps. A new definition would need a deliberate new binding rather than silent replacement.

limitations: The archive does not promise a persistent versioned registry.
The particular version/hash policy remains undecided.
validation_needed: A redefinition cannot reinterpret a prior assembly.
Conflicting registration is rejected or explicitly versioned.

entries.title: Frozen metadata has a specific boundary

source_evidence.observation: RegistryEntry freezes itself and its declared arrays; ordinary PipelineNode instances remain mutable apart from those arrays.

interpretation.text: Metadata immutability is useful but does not freeze the plugin implementation, runtime instance, context or registry binding.

application.text: Describe exactly which native values are immutable, and keep that guarantee separate from registry replacement and execution state.

limitations: A freeze operation is not a complete persistence or authority policy.
validation_needed: Mutations at each promised immutable boundary are rejected.
Execution configuration is captured separately from mutable UI state.

entries.title: Keep environment adapters separate from processing

source_evidence.observation: Browser elements are wrapped in provider/sink objects.
The reader plugin receives a provider rather than reading DOM elements directly.

interpretation.text: The boundary lets processing logic be considered separately from the browser interface.

application.text: Use explicit interfaces for native input, reference resolution and publication, with their own typed contracts. Keep a future inspector outside authoritative processing logic.

limitations: The supplied adapters are browser-specific.
A provider interface alone does not validate its data.
validation_needed: Substituting an input/output mechanism preserves the declared semantic result.
Invalid adapter envelopes are rejected consistently.

entries.title: Explicit entry and terminal sentinels clarify a pass

source_evidence.observation: START and STOP are fixed system nodes with diagnostic behavior.
A pass is bracketed and checked for unique instance IDs and valid interior node types.

interpretation.text: Visible boundaries make a planned pass easier to inspect. The StopNode terminates traversal of that pass; it is not the runtime STOP signal or a durable commit.

application.text: Give future assembly/execution plans explicit boundaries and terminal outcomes without conflating traversal completion, publication and commit.

limitations: The sentinel is not a transaction boundary.
Per-character dispatch should not be inferred from processor sentinels.
validation_needed: A failed or interrupted pass cannot claim a successful terminal outcome.

entries.title: An inspectable ordered stage list is an assembly structure

source_evidence.observation: Loaded stage occurrences can be inserted, removed and moved.
The UI displays ordered occurrence identities and declared metadata.

interpretation.text: Ordering can be represented and inspected as data. This list assembles processors; it does not represent word or paragraph composition.

application.text: Make a future processing plan inspectable before execution, and snapshot its exact ordered identities/configuration. Keep native content assembly as a separate structure.

limitations: The current list is live mutable state.
Changing visible order is not proof that the order is valid.
validation_needed: Reordering creates an explicit plan revision.
A running plan remains bound to its captured definition.

entries.title: Dependency warnings are not execution preconditions

source_evidence.observation: Missing and misordered dependencies are returned as warnings.
Pipeline validation logs dependency warnings without rejecting execution.

interpretation.text: A processor may run without a producer it declared necessary. Diagnostics alone do not establish valid dataflow.

application.text: Define which dependencies are mandatory, validate them before authoritative execution, and report an invalid plan rather than silently using stale/default state.

limitations: Warning-only behavior can be suitable for a permissive demonstrator.
The native dependency contract is not defined by this archive.
validation_needed: Remove or reorder a required stage and verify a declared rejection before mutation/publication.

entries.title: Repeated types require occurrence-aware dependency checks

source_evidence.observation: Dependency ordering compares the first occurrence of each type rather than the current record's position.

interpretation.text: With repeated dependent types, a later instance can be assessed against an earlier instance's position. The code does not specify which producer occurrence supplies which consumer.

application.text: Bind repeated processors to explicit predecessor/output occurrences or a declared selection rule. Do not infer dataflow solely from matching type names.

limitations: The problematic runtime sequence has not been executed.
Different dependency semantics may intentionally require an early producer.
validation_needed: Exercise repeated producers/consumers on both sides of a required stage and compare with the declared occurrence-binding rule.

entries.title: Declared support labels do not establish a data contract

source_evidence.observation: Support metadata is a string list.
Execution invokes a node without validating declared input/output shapes or checking a support label against context data.

interpretation.text: A JSON/universal label is useful discovery metadata but not a schema, semantic guarantee or native codepage contract.

application.text: Specify accepted native structures, produced structures, map versions and failure behavior for each coarse processing operation.

limitations: Individual supplied plugins perform some local checks.
No universal type system should be inferred from enum names.
validation_needed: Mismatched inputs and invalid outputs fail at their declared boundary.

entries.title: Discovery metadata and activation are different operations

source_evidence.observation: Installation constructs a real plugin to obtain its metadata.
Loading constructs another instance.

interpretation.text: A constructor may be invoked during discovery and again during activation. Future constructor side effects would therefore run at both stages; the supplied examples do not demonstrate harmful effects.

application.text: Consider inert definition records for discovery and explicit activation of an execution occurrence. Keep native unit lookup free of processor startup.

limitations: The example constructors mostly initialize metadata and validate arguments.
No external plugin was installed or executed in this review.
validation_needed: Listing definitions performs no hidden I/O or execution.
Activation side effects occur only at the declared boundary.

entries.title: Linear recursive traversal is not hierarchical content assembly

source_evidence.observation: Recursion advances through a flat node array.
The README describes a start/plugins/stop runtime shape.

interpretation.text: The word recursive does not establish reusable child assemblies, graph references, word/sentence composition or memoized substructure.

application.text: Define native assembly explicitly with its own unit/child relationships and cycle rules. Use processing traversal only for processing traversal.

limitations: This is not a claim that the source intended to implement a native document graph.
validation_needed: A future hierarchical assembler preserves ordered children, shared definitions and the declared cycle/depth policy.

entries.title: Shared mutable context changes the history model

source_evidence.observation: A run owns a mutable object with data, derived states, output, stream, diagnostics and errors.
A processor writes its result into the input data object.

interpretation.text: Later stages can overwrite content or derived state. This differs from immutable input/output values and addressable historical transformations.

application.text: Preserve immutable native inputs and explicit resulting assemblies. Keep derived measurements separate from authoritative content and bind them to an input identity.

limitations: Mutable context is convenient for a small browser demo.
Cloned output snapshots do not provide a complete durable lineage model.
validation_needed: Earlier assemblies remain byte/semantically unchanged after later operations.
Derived analysis cannot alter its source content.

entries.title: Analysis tokens are not a complete native document stream

source_evidence.observation: The matcher collects word/symbol tokens and omits whitespace from its token list.

interpretation.text: Tokens may support analysis while failing to encode spaces, returns and all native units as ordered entries. Original text is still available in context; the token list alone is not established as lossless.

application.text: Keep every required native unit/control reference in authoritative assemblies. Derive analytical token views separately when useful.

limitations: The archive describes tokenization for analysis rather than a lossless codec.
Native return semantics remain an explicit design question.
validation_needed: Reconstruct text/control structure from native references without consulting discarded whitespace.
Analysis leaves the original assembly unchanged.

entries.title: Convenience normalization can alter source content

source_evidence.observation: Plain-text input is trimmed before JSON detection or wrapping as text.

interpretation.text: Leading/trailing whitespace can be removed and JSON-looking text can be reinterpreted as a value. These are meaningful transformations if input is authoritative text.

application.text: Make the input kind explicit. Preserve native content and record any requested normalization as a transformation with a defined policy.

limitations: Trimming can be an intentional UI convenience; it is unsuitable as an implicit native-source rule.
validation_needed: Leading/trailing spaces, blank content and JSON-looking literal text retain their intended identities.

entries.title: Coordinates need an explicit meaning

source_evidence.observation: Token start/end use JavaScript string positions and lengths; no coordinate-unit contract accompanies the fields.
Regex results also expose string positions.

interpretation.text: A numeric offset cannot automatically be treated as a native unit reference, displayed character index or stable historical target.

application.text: Declare coordinate units and their input-version binding wherever text ranges coexist with native references.

limitations: No Unicode position conversion was executed in this review.
The future native coordinate scheme is not chosen here.
validation_needed: Combining sequences, supplementary characters and edits preserve declared addressing behavior.

entries.title: Derived frequency indexes have their own rules and key domain

source_evidence.observation: Frequency keys are folded to lowercase and stored in a normal object accumulator.

interpretation.text: Case-insensitive statistics do not define canonical character identity. User-derived keys such as inherited object-property names also need deliberate dictionary semantics.

application.text: Bind derived indexes to an assembly and explicit analysis policy. Use a key representation that handles every permitted native value without inherited-property ambiguity.

limitations: The original token.value retains its case.
Prototype-key effects are predicted from the accumulator structure, not runtime-tested exploits.
validation_needed: Mixed case remains distinct in authoritative content.
Keys such as constructor and __proto__ are handled as ordinary data under the declared counting policy.

entries.title: Valid falsy values require consistent boundary treatment

source_evidence.observation: The fallback substitutes an empty object for falsy data.
Counting replaces non-object/falsy content with an object before adding its result.
The file/text JSON parsing paths are not limited to object roots by a subsequent plain-object check.

interpretation.text: Input modes and downstream assumptions disagree for values such as false, zero or null. Absence and a legitimate value should have different rules.

application.text: Define the accepted native envelope and preserve every valid value. Reject unsupported shapes explicitly instead of silently replacing them.

limitations: This review did not execute the affected JSON inputs.
validation_needed: All input modes agree on object/primitive acceptance.
Valid zero/false/empty values are not confused with missing data.

entries.title: Result caps do not bound a single regex evaluation

source_evidence.excerpt: if(source.length>500) throw new RangeError("Regex source too long.");
source_evidence.observation: The helper validates length and flags before creating a native RegExp.
Execution is synchronous; the match cap is checked only after exec returns.

interpretation.text: The name safe and the match-count limit do not establish a runtime deadline or interrupt a slow evaluation.

application.text: If regex analysis is retained, specify input/pattern limits and a genuinely enforceable execution budget. Keep it optional around native assemblies.

limitations: No pathological expression was executed.
Actual engine behavior must be measured within an approved worker/timeout scope.
validation_needed: A slow expression terminates within its deadline without blocking authoritative service work.

entries.title: Bounded scanners need correct progress and honest completion

source_evidence.observation: Zero-length matches manually advance the index; scans stop at maxMatches, but the result has no truncated/completion field.

interpretation.text: A scanner must both make valid progress in its coordinate model and distinguish a complete result from a capped prefix.

application.text: Declare continuation/completion and coordinate rules for analytical scans. Do not let a capped analysis masquerade as complete assembly knowledge.

limitations: Unicode zero-width cases were not executed.
The match cap itself is a useful resource mechanism.
validation_needed: Test empty matches, supplementary characters and exact-cap versus over-cap scans.
A partial result advertises its completeness state.

entries.title: Analysis can be keyed by its processing occurrence

source_evidence.observation: Each loaded regex instance receives its own result slot.
Results retain pattern/flags, source length, match data and execution time.

interpretation.text: Distinct analysis occurrences can coexist. An occurrence ID and timestamp alone do not bind the result to immutable content or prove replay equivalence.

application.text: Address derived analysis by occurrence plus exact input identity, definition/configuration identity and declared result status.

limitations: This state is session-local and mutable.
Regex analysis is not a native unit definition.
validation_needed: Two analyses preserve their own identities and cannot be attached to the wrong assembly revision.

entries.title: Periodic polling and change-driven work have different costs

source_evidence.observation: The runtime uses a fixed delay.
While running, each loop schedules another pass without an input-change test.

interpretation.text: A repeating demo is easy to observe but may redo tokenization/search/publication for unchanged input. The source has no demonstrated content/profile cache or operation reduction.

application.text: Choose explicit batch/change boundaries and reuse results whose inputs and processing definitions are unchanged. Measure polling separately if a future source actually requires it.

limitations: The 300 ms value is not a measured latency requirement.
No performance benchmark was run.
validation_needed: Unchanged inputs avoid unnecessary construction/rendering.
A changed dependency invalidates only the results it actually affects.

entries.title: A visible run state is not a single-flight guard

source_evidence.observation: runOnce sets state but does not reject or serialize an already running call.
The UI handler invokes the same runtime; it has no per-run exclusion flag.

interpretation.text: Overlapping calls can interleave when a stage awaits, because shared context and lifecycle state are reused. Actual overlap has not been exercised.

application.text: Specify owner/queue/concurrency behavior and bind each accepted execution to a unique immutable plan and request outcome.

limitations: Synchronous stages do not yield to another button handler during their own body.
No concurrency test was run against this archive.
validation_needed: Submit concurrent runs around an asynchronous reader and confirm declared serialization or explicit rejection.

entries.title: Lifecycle signals need completion-generation rules

source_evidence.observation: Pause/stop are checked between nodes.
The returned context is assigned after awaited work; completion returns state to running unless error/stop conditions apply.
Reset replaces context without invalidating an in-flight completion generation.

interpretation.text: A late completion can conflict with a pause/reset request. Cooperative signal checks also cannot interrupt a synchronous long-running node.

application.text: Define legal state transitions, execution generations and cancellation points. Reject stale completion and use owned workers where interruption must be enforceable.

limitations: Timing-dependent pause/reset effects remain predicted, not reproduced.
A terminal sentinel is distinct from cancellation of a running operation.
validation_needed: Pause/reset during an awaited node cannot resurrect old state.
Stop and timeout have bounded, truthful outcomes.

entries.title: Bound all retained run state rather than only the debug log

source_evidence.observation: The debug log has a retention count.
Stream entries and diagnostics accumulate without an equivalent byte/count bound; output includes the growing diagnostics array.

interpretation.text: A bounded debug log does not bound total retained state. Repeated serialized diagnostic histories can amplify storage growth across passes.

application.text: Specify retention, backpressure and durable history independently. Use stable references for repeated material rather than incidental copies of a growing diagnostic history.

limitations: No long-duration memory or storage measurements were taken.
Diagnostic history is different from authoritative transformation history.
validation_needed: A bounded soak accounts for all retained collections and bytes.
History preservation and resource caps have an explicit compatibility policy.

entries.title: Publication and its evidence require a consistent boundary

source_evidence.observation: The plugin builds/clones output and calls the sink before appending its output-written diagnostic.
The supplied sink copies and displays output in memory.

interpretation.text: The emitted snapshot does not include that pass's later output-written diagnostic. A successful browser display does not establish a durable artifact or an atomic head/receipt transition.

application.text: Keep construction, publication, verification and commit outcomes distinct, and make the evidence correspond to the exact boundary it claims.

limitations: The source is an in-memory display, not a durable storage service.
No crash/restart publication test was run.
validation_needed: Failure around publication cannot claim ready output or advance a guarded head.
Diagnostics identify whether they describe intent, completion or verified persistence.

entries.title: Multiple state fields need one truthful outcome contract

source_evidence.observation: The catch block appends an error and changes runtime.state without assigning context.status.
The usual context.status update is skipped on the error path.

interpretation.text: Runtime state and context status can disagree after a failure. If output is not reached, a UI may also retain an earlier successful display.

application.text: Define an authoritative terminal outcome and bind displayed artifacts/status to the specific execution occurrence. Keep prior successful output identifiable as prior output.

limitations: This is a predicted state-consistency issue from static branches, not an executed UI defect.
validation_needed: A failing stage produces consistent runtime, result, receipt and displayed-output state.

entries.title: Telemetry, repeatability and attestation are separate claims

source_evidence.observation: Logs contain timestamps and cloned metadata.
Run identity is generated in memory; the archive has no durable receipt or sealed-plan mechanism.

interpretation.text: A readable log helps diagnose a run but does not prove input identity, deterministic semantics, durable completion or independent attestation.

application.text: Bind evidence to input/definition/plan/result identities and distinguish deterministic payload from execution telemetry. Keep proof claims within their measured boundary.

limitations: Hashing or UUIDs alone would not establish authority or truth.
The archive is not claimed to be an attestation system.
validation_needed: Replay compares the promised deterministic material while retaining separate timing/run metadata.

entries.title: Copying and naming checks do not establish an immutable safe boundary

source_evidence.observation: The README describes hardened cloning with multiple supported types and explicit rejections.
A built-in clone is tried before a manual fallback.
Fallback retains prototypes/property descriptors; assertPlainObject only rejects null, non-objects and arrays.

interpretation.text: A clone can isolate some mutation while retaining mutable objects, prototypes and accessor behavior. A helper called plain or hardened does not by itself establish a strict data schema or execution containment.

application.text: Prefer explicit allowed native value shapes and immutable ownership rules. Adopt only the copy behavior that an actual boundary requires, with declared graph/host-type semantics.

limitations: No malicious object or host value was executed.
JSON-parsed data and live plugin objects have different risk/semantic domains.
validation_needed: Check accessors, prototypes, unsupported objects and consistent behavior across clone paths.
Validate shapes rather than relying on helper names.

entries.title: Plugin categories do not isolate execution authority

source_evidence.observation: An external-plugin category is declared.
Factories are called as JavaScript constructors in the same environment.
Plugins receive the runtime and shared context; no separate execution boundary is created.

interpretation.text: The provided model suits trusted packaged processors. A category label does not make arbitrary extensions contained or safe to activate.

application.text: Declare processor authority and trust separately from catalogue metadata. A future extension boundary would need its own explicit design and approval.

limitations: There is no demonstrated arbitrary-file upload or dynamic remote plugin installer in the supplied UI.
No containment test was attempted.
validation_needed: Document exactly which operations each installed processor may perform and how those limits are enforced.

entries.title: Inspection views can stay separate from authoritative output

source_evidence.observation: The browser displays serialized data as text.
A separate analysis action writes the output pane without executing the configured pipeline.

interpretation.text: A read/analysis view can be useful independently of a pipeline run. Sharing one pane also needs clear provenance so an inspection result is not mistaken for committed content.

application.text: Offer version-bound inspections with explicit result kinds and input identities. Keep displaying diagnostic text separate from interpreting native HTML constructs.

limitations: textContent use is a local display mechanism, not proof of a whole-application security boundary.
The out-of-band result is not catalogued durably.
validation_needed: Inspection never advances a content head and remains labeled with its source revision and purpose.

entries.title: An inspector's presentation is not a document renderer contract

source_evidence.observation: The page provides status and textual output/debug panes.
The stylesheet supplies responsive grid changes and environment-selected UI/monospace font stacks.

interpretation.text: The layout can inspire an inspection interface, but it does not establish pinned document fonts, pagination, pixel equivalence or native rendering definitions.

application.text: Keep a future inspector's ergonomics separate from the reproducible rendering profile and authoritative native data model.

limitations: The UI was not opened or visually assessed in this review.
CSS appearance is not an acceptance requirement for Docstream.
validation_needed: If an inspector is proposed later, assess usability separately from document rendering fidelity.

entries.title: Edifice: a packaged browser pipeline demonstrator

source_evidence.observation: Six classic scripts compose the core, adapters, plugins and UI in a fixed order.
The application creates browser providers, a runtime, an installed catalogue and a default stage list.
The default list reads, tokenizes, searches, passes through, counts and outputs.

interpretation.text: Its whole composition is a locally packaged, inspectable processing demonstration with mutable in-memory state. Useful component arrangements do not transfer every operating assumption.

application.text: Use the edifice as a comparative design reference. Select boundaries and identity lessons individually against Docstream's native, immutable and durable requirements.

limitations: The archive's README instruction to open a browser is source material, not authorization; it was not followed.
This review establishes no successful boot or runtime behavior.
validation_needed: Any future adoption proposal identifies the precise component, required adaptation and acceptance boundary.

entries.title: Edifice boundary: the native reference data plane is still a separate design

source_evidence.observation: The context has generic data and analysis state rather than declared native unit/reference/assembly records.
The supplied analytical model consists of strings, positions, token classes and frequencies.

interpretation.text: Across the nine reviewed files, no module implements the user's direct native character/unit catalogue, location resolver and reusable word/sentence/paragraph assemblies. A processor registry cannot stand in for that data plane.

application.text: Design native units/references/assemblies explicitly. Process those structures at coarse stages; character resolution should remain a data operation with a declared identity contract.

limitations: This absence statement is limited to the supplied archive.
It does not prescribe reference width, mandatory word interning or per-language semantics.
validation_needed: A later native-core proposal identifies primitive definitions, resolver behavior, assembly ordering and representation binding.

entries.title: A version label and README claims are not validation evidence

source_evidence.observation: The README labels the package v7 and describes hardened cloning and an insertable regex plugin.
The supplied usage instruction is not a retained successful execution record.

interpretation.text: The archive inventory contains nine files and no packaged test suite or validation report. Static findings and named capabilities must not be presented as tested guarantees.

application.text: Keep source claim, static evidence, predicted effect, approved adaptation and executed validation distinct. Validate only a separately authorized concrete adaptation.

limitations: Tests or reports may exist elsewhere; this catalogue does not establish their absence globally.
The review has not run the source through Docstream's harness.
validation_needed: Any future runtime claim has retained inputs, outcomes, failure cases and environment identity.

entries.title: Selective adaptation is a traceable design operation

source_evidence.observation: The source provides a reusable definition/occurrence distinction.
Environment boundaries are explicit components.
The same composition also contains behavior that does not meet a strict execution contract.

interpretation.text: Useful ideas and unsuitable assumptions coexist in the same source. Preserving that distinction is more informative than accepting or rejecting the whole package.

application.text: For any future adaptation, name the catalogue entries used, new requirements, rejected assumptions, exact component boundaries and validation. Write the resulting design for this project rather than copying a class tree or default pipeline.

limitations: This record is a method for future proposals, not approval to implement them.
No source classes, plugin defaults or UI have been integrated.
validation_needed: A design decision traces to evidence while stating what changed and what was deliberately not adopted.
Existing immutable/durable behavior remains within its own acceptance requirements.

entries.title: A no-content-change stage can still be an observable occurrence

source_evidence.observation: The plugin's own diagnostic declares no data mutation.
The body appends diagnostics, logs a pass-through event and returns the same context, with no direct assignment to context.data.

interpretation.text: No-op is relative to authoritative content. A stage can preserve content while still having an occurrence, diagnostics and resource cost; its self-description is not an independent guarantee.

application.text: Retain requested transformation occurrences even when content is unchanged or execution is reduced away. Check semantic equality separately from lineage and telemetry.

limitations: The shared context still changes through diagnostics.
The archive does not provide a durable no-op lineage or conformance test.
validation_needed: A declared no-op preserves native content and retains a distinguishable occurrence.
Instrumentation changes do not masquerade as document changes.
